What it asks: Clear, comprehensive, accurate information; disclose charges, interest, total cost of credit, due date
How our design responds: Decline letter (11.6) and reason codes state the decision and its main factors in plain language; the cost model uses disclosed flat, non-compounded pricing
Status: Partly. Pricing disclosure is a product task outside the model

What it asks: Digital pre-agreement: principal, disbursement schedule, cost of default, fees, insurance
How our design responds: Scoring service returns the approved limit; pre-agreement content is outside the model
Status: Not met by the model; product must supply it

What it asks: Interest disclosed for the tenure, not compounded
How our design responds: Cost matrix (src/costs.py) uses a flat fee rate; no compounding

What it asks: Complaint receipt and resolution within twenty days
How our design responds: Decline letter gives a complaint channel and the 20-day commitment
Status: Met in the letter; NkwaPay must run the process

What it asks: No harassment, threats, or contacting a customer's contacts during collection
How our design responds: The model uses no contact-list or social data, and recovery assumptions do not rely on such tactics

What it asks: Submit customer credit information to licensed bureaus daily, with prior customer consent
How our design responds: Not in scope of the model; bureau data is recommended as a future feature (Part C)
Status: Not met: no bureau integration in our system

What it asks: Accountability, lawful and reasonable processing, purpose specification, openness, security, participation
How our design responds: Model Card documents purpose, data and limits; features are restricted to loan application and repayment records
Status: Partly. Security and accountability processes are organisational

What it asks: Minimality: processing necessary, relevant and not excessive
How our design responds: Calendar and macro features removed (no predictive value); leaky columns dropped; no special or social data used

What it asks: Consent or lawful basis; specific purpose; data subject made aware
How our design responds: Credit assessment is necessary for the contract (s.20(1)(a)); notice of purpose is in the letter
Status: Partly. Consent capture is a product task

What it asks: Quality of information: complete, accurate, up to date
How our design responds: Leakage audit (Section 1) found Total_Amount_to_Repay updated after default; excluded

What it asks: Access to personal data; correction of inaccurate data
How our design responds: Letter tells the applicant how to request their data and correct errors; reason codes show which records drove the decision
Status: Met in the letter; NkwaPay must handle requests

What it asks: Special personal data (religion, ethnicity, race, health, politics, etc.) not processed
Automated decisions that significantly affect a person: notify, and reconsider on request within 21 days; s.41(4)(a)-(b) exempts decisions about entering into a contract
How our design responds: Credit approval arguably falls under the contract exemption, but we design as if s.41 applies: the letter notifies the automated basis and offers human reconsideration within 21 days
Status: Met by design (stronger than the minimum)

What it asks: Credit-bureau data subject rights; retention under Act 726 s.30 (as cited in Act 843 s.36)
Status: Not applicable until bureau integration; text of Act 726 not reviewed

What it asks: Reportedly: lenders must obtain a credit report before granting credit
How our design responds: Our model does not query a bureau
Status: Likely not met; must be confirmed against the Act's text

What it asks: Digital credit policy in line with the Borrowers and Lenders Act 2020 (Act 1052)
